item.title: Stable Configurations of Dark Energy Stars in f(R,L_m,T) Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.09983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the context of $f(R,L_m,T)$ gravity, two analytical solutions are proposed in this study, representing the structure of compact spherical objects whose behavior is dominated by dark energy fluid parameters. The extended field equations are derived using a static interior spacetime under the considered model which characterize a geometric structure including both dark energy and ordinary matter. The field equations are solved using the connections between dark energy with conventional matter, which are governed by different equations of state. This analysis further employs the Kohler-Chao-Tikekar and Durgapal-Fluoria spacetimes as two distinct ansatzes to close the system of field equations, resulting in two independent solutions. For both solutions, the constants are fixed by matching the interior and exterior spacetimes at the boundary using junction conditions. This study also assesses the proposed models using data from SAX J1808.4-3658, and explore the implications of varying the parametric values within the standard modified framework. The analysis concludes that both models fulfil the necessary physical conditions to ensure their candidacy for realistic stellar structures.
item.dc:creator: M. Sharif, Tayyab Naseer, Aqsa Bashir

item.title: Zeroth law of black hole mechanics in general Horndeski theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.09984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the validity of the zeroth law in the general class of scalar-tensor theories with second-order field equations, namely Horndeski theories or generalized Galileon theories in four-dimensional spacetime. Assuming that the non-minimally coupled scalar field inherits the spacetime symmetries, we show that the horizon mixed projection of the field equations implies constant surface gravity on a stationary Killing horizon. Our analysis incorporates the most generic non-minimal scalar couplings permitted within the Horndeski framework, which we consider as a perturbative expansion about general relativity. Our results therefore classify the possible cases within this framework of proof for different classes of scalar-tensor theories, including shift-symmetric scalar fields. These results extend the applicability of black hole mechanics beyond Einstein gravity and provide further evidence for the thermodynamic consistency of general Horndeski theories.
item.dc:creator: Ribhu Paul, Krishnakanta Bhattacharya

item.title: One-Particle Equivalence of Lorentz-Violating and Lorentz-Deformed Theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.09986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Planck-scale departures from special relativity are commonly described by theories that break Lorentz symmetry and theories in which such symmetry is deformed. We prove that, under a global shell-linearizability condition, these two descriptions are physically equivalent for a single particle, corresponding to unitarily equivalent realizations of the same Wigner orbit expressed in different momentum coordinates. This equivalence breaks down for multiparticle systems, except when the momentum-composition law can be reduced to the ordinary addition of momenta. Our results imply that the distinction between Lorentz violating and Lorentz-deformed kinematics can only be tested by genuine multiparticle observables. We discuss Compton edge measurements as a prototype example of such a multiparticle probe.
item.dc:creator: Arshid Shabir, Francesco Marino, Mir Faizal

item.title: Finite-amplitude wave dynamics in weak-field-equivalent nonlinear electrodynamics in $(2+1)$ dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine finite-amplitude wave propagation in $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlinear electrodynamics using Born-Infeld, logarithmic, and quadratic polynomial models whose Lagrangians agree through quadratic order in the electromagnetic invariant. Despite this weak-field agreement, characteristic and linearized analyses on homogeneous magnetic background reveal distinct propagation speeds and hyperbolicity domains. In the weak-background limit, the first coefficient at which Lagrangians differ also controls the leading nonlinear variation of the simple-wave characteristic velocity. Exact right-moving simple-waves, corroborated by finite-volume evolution, show rigid Born-Infeld propagation but finite-time gradient catastrophes in the logarithmic and polynomial models, substantially earlier in the latter for matched pulses. These catastrophes can occur while the field remains finite and the system remains hyperbolic, showing that weak-field agreement does not determine finite-amplitude dynamics.
item.dc:creator: M. L. Pe\~nafiel, E. Veneros, A. Urquidi

item.title: A Heuristic Mirror-Bulk Model of Schwarzschild Black Hole Interiors
item.description: arXiv:2505.00732v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Schwarzschild -- non-rotating and chargeless -- black holes (BHs) are classically understood to be voids of extreme gravitation, with modern and contemporary apporaches having involved string-theoretical black branes and superfluid analogs. In this study, we reconsider Schwarzschild BHs by letting its black brane be a closed spherical surface, within which a mirror-bulk fluid is contained, mirrored by surface-dwelling Hawking radiation quanta. By employing a once-used variational method of solving the Einstein field equations, the eneregtic output is approximated by the metric Ansatz input. Here, we consider a Tangherlini-like black 2-brane metric Ansatz in 3+1 spacetime, and via $G_{\mu\nu}=8\pi GT_{\mu\nu}$ the geometric information of the time-time component $G_{00}$ determines the corresponding (effective) energy density $T_{00}$ and the respective energy profile $E:=T_{00}V$. These are found to be functions of the radial coordinate, which also applies to the BH interior $r\in[0,~r_S]$. We explore and discuss the mirror-bulk energy content, internal pressure, and the mass- and pressure-gradients of a mirror-bulk BH.
item.dc:creator: Noah M. MacKay

item.title: Natural Lithopanspermia to Earth: Transport, Shielding, and Survival Limits for Solar-System and Extrasolar Donor Classes
item.description: arXiv:2604.03916v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Natural panspermia is a transport-and-establishment hypothesis, not a theory of abiogenesis. The Earth-specific question is whether any nonterrestrial donor remains competitive with terrestrial origin once launch, planetary-system escape, transit, Earth interception, atmospheric entry, terminal loading, and post-delivery establishment are imposed. We formulate this problem as a donor-class dependent Earth-directed transport-survival kernel, supplemented by a minimum protected-depth envelope d_{min}(t_{flight}) and a survival-weighted buried-volume fraction F_{bur} for the low-shock spall population. The resulting hierarchy is strongly ordered under current transport and survival constraints. Hard panspermia is physically credible only on Solar-System scales: early Mars combines demonstrated lithic exchange with Earth, low escape speed, early aqueous habitability, and a rare 10^2-10^4 yr transfer tail, whereas the more common 10^5-10^7 yr martian transfer regime requires lightly shocked meter-class carriers. Beyond the Solar System, low-v_{inf} capture and long-duration survival fail simultaneously; even the Solar birth-cluster channel yields only ~3 x 10^{-5} f_{seed} expected Earth-seeding events, where f_{seed} is the conditional probability that a viable arrival establishes life on Earth. Indigenous terrestrial origin therefore remains the default inference, early Mars is the only quantitatively serious external hard-panspermia alternative, and extrasolar or intergalactic hard panspermia is not competitive for Earth's actual origin history. Soft panspermia is much more plausible as chemical enrichment of early terrestrial abiogenesis.
item.dc:creator: Slava G. Turyshev

item.title: Fluctuations in Aharonov-Bohm Electrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2604.15913v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the application of the Fluctuation Dissipation Theorem (FDT) to the electrodynamics of Aharonov-Bohm (ABE), which differs from Maxwell's in that it allows for local non-conservation of charge. For the case of a system of non-conserved charges at thermal equilibrium we obtain the same spectral distribution of energy of the electromagnetic field as in Maxwell electrodynamics. However, the electric field contribution to that energy doubles that in Maxwell case, while the magnetic contribution is the same as in Maxwell theory, the electric excess energy is compensated by a negative contribution arising form the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) scalar field. For a conductor with local non-conservation of charge described by the $\gamma$ model, we derive the spectrum of current correlation at first order in $\gamma$, which results in a violet noise contribution added to the classical Johnson-Nyquist white noise result for the voltage fluctuations in a conductor.
item.dc:creator: F. Minotti, G. Modanese

item.title: Joos-Weinberg covariant field with mass and spin $\frac{3}{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2605.28877v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the explicit theory of the Joos-Weinberg covariant field with spin $\frac{3}{2}$ which is a eight-dimensional massive covariant field transforming according to the representation $(\frac{3}{2},0)\oplus(0, \frac{3}{2})$ of the group $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$. As the transformation matrices of this representation are still unknown, we apply a new method for deriving them using exclusively maximally reducible representations, e. g. $(1,0)\otimes(\frac{1}{2},0)$ instead of the irreducible one $(1,\frac{1}{2})=(1,0)\otimes(0,\frac{1}{2})$ we meet in usual frameworks. After applying this method, we obtain a $12$-component covariant field transforming according to the representation $[(1,0)\otimes(\frac{1}{2},0)]\oplus [(0,1)\otimes(0, \frac{1}{2})]$ which is maximally reducible, up to subspaces of irreducible representations of the $SU(2)$ group. Consequently, after developing the theory in the direct product basis of the representation $(1,0)\otimes(\frac{1}{2},0)$, we can separate the sector of spin half revealing thus the genuine Joos-Weinberg covariant massive field of spin $\frac{3}{2}$. The theory of this field is build naturally deriving the field equation and associated matrices, Lagrangian formalism, inner product and the closed expressions of the orthonormal mode spinors.
item.dc:creator: Ion I. Cotaescu

item.title: Dark matter deformations of photon-ring echoes in horizon-scale interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2608.23591v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Photon-ring echoes can probe the delayed light paths near rotating black holes, even when their main ring scales agree. We study an effective rotating geometry with a strong dark matter spike and compare it with a separately ring-matched Kerr control. At $a/M_B=0.8$, $i=70^\circ$, and $M_H/M_B=10$, the remaining angular critical-parameter fingerprint is $1.49\%$. The first two higher image orders have median delays of $13.33M$ and $33.06M$, with spike--Kerr shifts of $1.192M$ and $0.378M$. Finite-order ray transport, slow-light synchrotron images, and complex very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) visibilities show distinct delay and interference patterns. Direct and higher-order images contribute differently to the complex visibility signal. With the same emitting source, the model difference survives controlled station noise. Independent synthetic-source tests show that the signal depends strongly on source variability: EHT-like held-out closures give an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of $0.658$ (95\% interval $0.497$--$0.807$), while two source-conditioned tests give AUC values close to $0.5$. Published general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) light curves of Sgr A* illustrate how electron physics changes variability on the relevant time scales. Together these results connect environmental photon transport to interferometric observables and quantify the importance of source information for future echo studies.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Fathi
